title: Active and Passive Voice, Direct and Reported Speech
summary: Changing sentences between active and passive voice in different tenses, and converting direct speech to reported (indirect) speech with changes to tense, pronouns and time words.

items: **Active voice**: the subject **does** the action. *The learners **cleaned** the classroom.*
**Passive voice**: the subject **receives** the action. *The classroom **was cleaned** by the learners.*

notes.text: To change active to passive: (1) the **object** becomes the new **subject**; (2) use the correct form of **to be** in the **same tense** + the **past participle**; (3) the old subject may follow 'by' (or be left out).

rows: The report **is being written** by Thabo.
The report **was being written** by Thabo.
The report **has been written** by Thabo.
The report **had been written** by Thabo.
The report **will be written** by Thabo.
The report **must be written** by Thabo.

notes.label: When is the passive useful?
notes.text: When the doer is unknown or unimportant (*My phone was stolen*), in scientific and formal writing (*The solution was heated*), and in news headlines. Too much passive voice makes writing dull, so prefer the active voice in most writing.

notes.title: Active to passive
notes.problem: Change to passive: 'The learners cleaned the classroom.'
steps: The object, 'the classroom', becomes the subject.
notes.answer: 'The classroom was cleaned by the learners.'

notes.text: **Direct speech** gives the exact words spoken, in inverted commas: *'I am tired,' said Zola.* **Reported (indirect) speech** reports what was said without quoting: *Zola said that she was tired.*

notes.caption: Changes when the reporting verb is in the past tense
rows: the next day / the previous day (the day before)

items: Remove the inverted commas and add **that** (for statements).
Change **pronouns** to suit the speaker: 'I' → he/she; 'my' → his/her; 'we' → they.

**Questions**: use *asked* + *if/whether* (yes/no questions) or the question word, and change to statement word order. *'Are you ready?' she asked.* → *She asked if I was ready.* *'Where do you live?' he asked.* → *He asked where I lived.*
**Commands**: use *told/ordered/asked* + *to*. *'Sit down,' said the teacher.* → *The teacher told us to sit down.*

notes.title: Converting to reported speech
notes.problem: 'I will finish this project tomorrow,' said Ayanda.
steps: I → she; will → would; this → that; tomorrow → the next day.
notes.answer: Ayanda said that she would finish that project the next day.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: The cat was chased by the dog.
The dog is chasing the cat.

questions.prompt: Change to the passive voice: 'The principal opened the new library.'
questions.memo:
✓ The new library was opened (1)
✓ by the principal. (1)

questions.prompt: Change to the passive voice: 'The workers are building a new bridge.'
questions.memo:
✓ A new bridge is being built (1)
✓ by the workers. (1)

questions.prompt: Change to the active voice: 'The match will be won by our team.'
questions.memo:
✓ Our team (1)
✓ will win the match. (1)

questions.prompt: In reported speech (after 'said'), what does 'will' usually become?
Match each direct-speech word to its reported-speech form.
Change to reported speech: 'I am writing my exam today,' said Kabelo.
questions.memo:
✓ Kabelo said that he (1)
✓ was writing his exam (1)
✓ that day. (1)

questions.prompt: Change to reported speech: 'Have you seen my keys?' Mom asked me.
questions.memo:
✓ Mom asked me if/whether (1)
✓ I had seen (1)
✓ her keys. (1)

questions.prompt: Change to reported speech: 'Hand in your books,' the teacher said to us.
questions.memo:
✓ The teacher told us (1)
✓ to hand in our books. (1)
